extraction.name: SWE-Gym
extraction.description: SWE-Gym is the first training environment combining real-world software engineering tasks from GitHub issues with pre-installed dependencies and executable test verification. It contains 2,438 real-world task instances, each comprising a Python codebase with an executable runtime environment, unit tests, and a task specified in natural language. The environment is designed to train language model-based software engineering (SWE) agents and verifiers, enabling scalable improvements in resolving complex software tasks.
extraction.creator: Jiayi Pan, Xingyao Wang, Graham Neubig, Navdeep Jaitly, Heng Ji, Alane Suhr, Yizhe Zhang
extraction.publisher: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267
extraction.citeAs: Jiayi Pan, Xingyao Wang, Graham Neubig, Navdeep Jaitly, Heng Ji, Alane Suhr, Yizhe Zhang. "Training Software Engineering Agents and Verifiers with SWE-Gym". arXiv:2412.21139v2 [cs.SE], 6 Jun 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: SWE-Gym contains 2,438 real-world task instances sourced from pull requests in 11 popular Python repositories. Tasks are extracted using SWE-Bench's instance extraction script, which converts repositories into task instances including natural language issue descriptions, repository snapshots, and unit tests. Executable environments are manually configured with pre-installed dependencies for each task instance, requiring approximately 200 human annotation hours and 10,000 CPU core hours. The gold patch (human-submitted code diff) is validated to pass more unit tests than the original code.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Physical data collection, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Real-world GitHub issues and associated code repositories from 11 popular open-source Python repositories. The raw data includes natural language issue descriptions, repository snapshots, and unit tests.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Tasks are filtered to ensure executable environments and effective unit tests. The gold patch is validated to pass more unit tests than the original code. Preprocessing includes manual configuration of dependencies for each task instance using relevant configuration files, CI scripts, or documentation from the repository snapshot at the time of issue creation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations are derived from human-written test suites that validate the correctness of code modifications. The unit tests serve as the ground truth for determining task success. Annotations are not explicitly authored by human annotators but are implicitly defined by the executable test verification process.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: SWE-Gym is publicly released with pre-built Docker images for each instance (totaling 6 TB). The dataset includes a subset SWE-Gym Lite (230 instances) for rapid prototyping. The authors plan to explore automatic environment synthesis and self-improvement with reinforcement learning in future work.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Improving automated software engineering capabilities could increase developer productivity and accessibility across industries. However, as these agents become more capable, they may impact software engineering jobs and require careful consideration around code ownership, licensing, and attribution. Additionally, while focused on legitimate software engineering tasks, similar techniques could potentially be misused to automate the creation of malicious code.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may exhibit biases due to the manual configuration of environments, which could introduce distribution bias. The success distribution over tasks is naturally biased toward easier tasks, as observed in the success rate distribution during sampling. Repository-level diversity is uneven, with tasks associated with pandas comprising nearly one-third of the total, while tasks related to bokeh represent only one percent.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: SWE-Gym is limited by its environment diversity, including the number of repositories, types of tasks, and programming languages. The dataset size and repository diversity are not yet bottlenecks, but further improvements could be achieved by allocating more computing resources to sampling more training trajectories. The dataset focuses solely on task completion, neglecting human-in-the-loop collaboration, which is essential for real-world software engineering.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and fine-tuning language model-based software engineering agents and verifiers. The dataset is used for training state-of-the-art open-weight SWE agents, enabling inference-time scaling through verifiers trained on agent trajectories. Use cases include automated software engineering, improving developer productivity, and supporting critical open-source infrastructure.
